To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chronic treatment with neurotrophin 3 enhances the potency and/or number of synapses from two different sources to motoneurons in the spinal cord of neonatal rats.
chronic exposure to neurotrophin 3 can enhance synaptic connections between motoneurons and their segmental and descending inputs in the spinal cord.

chronic NT- 3, delivered by implanted fibroblasts, enhances synaptic transmission to motoneurons, and that this effect differs from the acute enhancement of transmission that occurs with NT-3 application.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of neurotrophic factors (NTFs) in synaptic plasticity.
the role of neurotrophins, particularly NT-3, in the maturation of synaptic connections in the spinal cord of neonatal animals.
the effects of neurotrophins on the spinal cord.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chronic effect of NT-3 is to increase synaptic strength at connections not normally activated by the VLF input.
chronic exposure of the spinal cord to NT-3 enhances synaptic transmission to spinal motoneurons, and that this effect is mediated by mechanisms distinct from those underlying acute effects.
the chronic effects of NT-3 are not due to a change in NMDA receptor function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the NT-3 treatment enhances the synaptic transmission to the motoneurons by enhancing the efficacy of both segmental and descending pathways, and the efficacy of descending pathway is enhanced by both NMDA-dependent and -independent mechanisms.

NT-3 has a dual role in spinal cord development, enhancing synaptic transmission in the neonate, and enhancing the survival and function of motor and sensory neurons during development and in adulthood.
chronic NT- 3 treatment enhances synaptic transmission to spinal motoneurons by strengthening both segmental and descending inputs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chronic effect of NT-3 can occur at connections not activated by NMDA receptors at the time of treatment.
the effects of NT-3 are different depending on the duration of the exposure.
the effects of NT-3 on spinal cord function are long-term, and that these effects are not mediated by changes in NMDA receptor function.
